messages.subject: Registering brains
messages.body_plain:
Dear Adam,

On 16 Jul 2015, at 7:04, Adam Claridge-Chang wrote:

> I'm curious about how to register our own brains to a reference brain,
> is that something done in NAT, FIJI or VFB?

You can see bit.ly/flybrains <http://bit.ly/flybrains> for templates. FCWB is the template used
for FlyCircuit data, but I recommend JFRC2 if you have nc82 stained
brains.

For registration you can try https://github.com/jefferis/fiji-cmtk-gui
NB this only tested on a mac unfortunately. I recommend the Cachero 2010
registration parameters.

You can read much more about this in a CSH protocols articles that they
seem to have divided into 3

http://cshprotocols.cshlp.org/content/2013/4/pdb.prot071712.short

the staining and image registration ones are what you want. Note however
that the image registration GUI has been superseded by the one linked
above.

Best wishes,

Greg.

--
Gregory Jefferis, PhD
Division of Neurobiology
MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
Francis Crick Avenue
Cambridge Biomedical Campus
Cambridge, CB2 OQH, UK

http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/group-leaders/h-to-m/g-jefferis
http://jefferislab.org
http://flybrain.stanford.edu

messages.subject: Importing skeletonised neurons into NAT
messages.body_plain:
This seems like a basic question, but I can't seem to piece together from the documentation how to move from the skeletonised neuron data (which ImageJ outputs as csv data) to the RDA or SWC format favoured by the 'nat' package. Any little bit of help will be much appreciated!!

Gratitude in advance,
Joses

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Importing skeletonised neurons into NAT
messages.body_plain:
If you are using Fiji's simple neurite tracer plugin then you have the option to export as SWC (simplest) or in an XML format with extension .traces which is the plugin's native format.

Bay's read.neuron function understands both of these formats.

There is also a csv option but this loses all connectivity information and there is no direct support in read.neuron for this reason.

Best,

Greg.

Sent from my iPhone
